```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Pin 2026 quantifies the toxicity of six oral oncology drugs in human
small-intestinal organoids (hSIOs) with a cell-dynamics model, then carries the
organoid toxicity function into a human model of the small-intestinal
epithelium to predict villus injury and the probability of diarrhea at clinical
doses. The drugs are the CDK4/6 inhibitors abemaciclib and ribociclib and the
EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors poziotinib, lazertinib, mobocertinib and
osimertinib.

The paper contributes twelve model files: an organoid model and a human
epithelium model for each drug.

* `Pin_2026_<drug>_organoid` --- proliferative (MCM2+), non-proliferative and
  dead hSIO cells and toxic medium waste (Eqs 1-4), with the drug killing
  proliferative cells through a Hill function of the free drug concentration
  (Eqs 5-6). Parameters from Table 1.
* `Pin_2026_<drug>_human` --- the crypt-villus epithelium of Gall 2023 (stem,
  proliferative and non-proliferative crypt cells, villus cells, plus arrested
  and dead crypt and villus cells; Eqs E7-E15) driven by the same kill function
  at the free drug concentration in the crypt, and a cumulative-logit model of
  the probability of diarrhea of any grade and of grade 3 or higher
  (Eqs E16-E17).

In both models the drug exposure is the time-varying covariate `CEFFECT`
(free concentration at the site of action, uM). In the organoid it is the
measured medium concentration. In patients the authors used Simcyp V24 to
predict the free drug concentration in enterocytes (ileum I, M-ADAM), their
preferred surrogate for the crypt, and in plasma; that PBPK layer is not part of
the model files.

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Pin_2026_abemaciclib_human")()$reference`
* Article: [CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 15(5):e70256](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70256)

# Population

The organoid data come from one adult stem-cell-derived hSIO line from a single
donor (HUB Organoid Technology biobank), grown in serum-free medium and sampled
at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 h without medium refreshment, with 3-4 replicate wells
per drug concentration and a vehicle control on the same plates. MCM2+
proliferative and MCM2- non-proliferative cells were counted by
immunofluorescence image analysis.

The human epithelium is a typical-value model parametrised from human
small-intestine literature values (Table S3). Its diarrhea sub-model was fitted
to the reported diarrhea counts of 13 clinical-study arms of the six drugs
(Table 2): breast cancer for the CDK4/6 inhibitors and lung adenocarcinoma or
non-small cell lung cancer for the EGFR inhibitors.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
below collects the structure.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| hSIO cell dynamics (P, N, D, waste W) | Eqs 1-4 | Main text Eqs 1-4; deposited `HIOs_DynamicModel_Abema.m` |
| hSIO parameters per drug | `lambda_p`, `delta_pn`, `delta_nd`, `p_ref`, `n_ref`, initial values | Table 1 |
| Kill and arrest functions | `k * C^h / (C^h + C50^h)` | Eqs 5-6; Table 1 'Drug effects' |
| Human epithelium (S, P, D, V, arrested, dead) | Eqs E7-E14 | Supporting Information; deposited `GI_human_ODEs_Abema.m` |
| Steady-state-derived transfer rates | `delta_sp`, `delta_pd`, `delta_dv`, `tau_v` | Table S3 |
| Human cell-dynamics constants | `gamma = 3.41394`, `m = 1.468566`, `s_ss = 2`, `p_ss = 19.446`, `tau_Dead = ln(2)/12` | deposited `GI_human_Integr_Abema.m` (Table S3 prints other values, see below) |
| Crypt-to-villus crowding term | `((S+P+D)/(s_ss+p_ss+d_ss+C_Arr+C_Dead))^m` | deposited code (Eq E15 differs, see below) |
| Villus injury | `max(0, 1 - (V + V_Arr + V_Dead)/v_ss)` | Eq E16 |
| Diarrhea model | `P(grade <= k) = expit(g_k + r * I^h/(I^h + I_k^h))` | Eq E17; SAS NLMIXED output in the Supporting Information |
| Diarrhea estimates | `g0 = 1.7535`, `g2 = 6.2109`, `r_inj = -5.1074`, `I0 = 0.4818`, `I2 = 0.3998`, `h = 5` | Supporting Information SAS 'Parameter Estimates' |

# Organoid models: Figure 1

Figure 1C-H shows, for one representative concentration of each drug, the
fitted model for the vehicle and the treated wells on a `log10(1 + cells)` scale
over 96 h. The abemaciclib medium concentration was measured over the
experiment; the profile below is the deposited one (Data S2, `PK.mat`) at 24 h
spacing. For the other drugs the figure labels the concentration and the
medium is held constant at that value.

```{r organoid-setup}
abema_medium <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~c0.37, ~c1.1, ~c3.3, ~c10,
  0, 0.2990, 0.8438, 1.5775, 2.1550,
  24, 0.2710, 0.6948, 1.7725, 1.9550,
  48, 0.2492, 0.6398, 1.7750, 2.0075,
  72, 0.2655, 0.8597, 1.5525, 1.8975,
  96, 0.2655, 0.8598, 1.5525, 1.8975
)

# Concentration shown in each Figure 1 panel (uM).
fig1_conc <- c(
  ribociclib = 1.0, poziotinib = 0.0057, lazertinib = 0.06,
  mobocertinib = 0.037, osimertinib = 0.14
)

organoid_run <- function(drug, ceffect, params = NULL, tmax = 96) {
  mod <- readModelDb(paste0("Pin_2026_", drug, "_organoid"))
  if (!is.null(params)) {
    mod <- rxode2::ini(mod, params)
  }
  grid <- seq(0, tmax, by = 1)
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1, time = grid, evid = 0, cmt = "prolif",
    CEFFECT = ceffect(grid)
  )
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev, covsInterpolation = "linear", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8
  ))
}
const_conc <- function(value) function(t) rep(value, length(t))
abema_conc <- function(t) stats::approx(abema_medium$time, abema_medium$c3.3, t, rule = 2)$y

drugs <- c("abemaciclib", "ribociclib", "poziotinib", "lazertinib", "mobocertinib", "osimertinib")
fig1 <- lapply(drugs, function(drug) {
  # Figure 1C starts from about 553 proliferative and 230 non-proliferative
  # cells, not from the Table 1 abemaciclib inoculum (1993 / 1110); see the
  # assumptions section.
  ic <- if (drug == "abemaciclib") list(p0 = 553, n0 = 230) else NULL
  treated <- if (drug == "abemaciclib") abema_conc else const_conc(fig1_conc[[drug]])
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    dplyr::mutate(organoid_run(drug, const_conc(0), ic), arm = "Vehicle"),
    dplyr::mutate(organoid_run(drug, treated, ic), arm = "Drug")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = drug)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
```

```{r organoid-figure, fig.height = 7}
fig1 |>
  dplyr::select(drug, arm, time, lprolif, lnonprolif) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(lprolif, lnonprolif), names_to = "cells", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cells = dplyr::recode(cells, lprolif = "MCM2+ proliferative", lnonprolif = "MCM2- non-proliferative"),
    drug = factor(drug, levels = drugs)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(drug ~ cells) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Vehicle = "pink3", Drug = "royalblue3")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "log10(1 + cells)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1C-H of Pin 2026.") +
  theme_bw()
```

The 96-h model values read from the Figure 1 panels (to about 0.05 log units)
are compared with the packaged models below.

```{r organoid-check}
fig1_published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~arm, ~lprolif_pub, ~lnonprolif_pub,
  "abemaciclib", "Vehicle", 4.00, 3.60,
  "abemaciclib", "Drug", 3.25, 2.65,
  "ribociclib", "Vehicle", 3.85, 3.50,
  "ribociclib", "Drug", 3.80, 3.40,
  "poziotinib", "Vehicle", 3.25, 3.05,
  "poziotinib", "Drug", 2.15, 2.35,
  "lazertinib", "Vehicle", 3.25, 3.05,
  "lazertinib", "Drug", 2.95, 2.80,
  "mobocertinib", "Vehicle", 3.20, 3.05,
  "mobocertinib", "Drug", 2.10, 2.35,
  "osimertinib", "Vehicle", 3.65, 3.40,
  "osimertinib", "Drug", 2.50, 2.60
)
fig1_cmp <- fig1 |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 96) |>
  dplyr::select(drug, arm, lprolif, lnonprolif) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig1_published, by = c("drug", "arm")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    d_prolif = lprolif - lprolif_pub,
    d_nonprolif = lnonprolif - lnonprolif_pub
  )
fig1_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Drug = drug, Arm = arm,
    "Model log10(1+P)" = lprolif, "Figure log10(1+P)" = lprolif_pub,
    "Model log10(1+N)" = lnonprolif, "Figure log10(1+N)" = lnonprolif_pub,
    "Diff P" = d_prolif, "Diff N" = d_nonprolif
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Organoid cell counts at 96 h: packaged models versus Figure 1.")

# Panels C, D, E and G and the panel F vehicle arm agree to within the reading
# precision plus a small margin. The panel F drug arm and the panel H vehicle
# arm do not follow from Table 1 (see the assumptions section).
fig1_cg <- dplyr::filter(
  fig1_cmp,
  drug != "osimertinib",
  !(drug == "lazertinib" & arm == "Drug")
)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(fig1_cg$d_prolif)) < 0.2,
  max(abs(fig1_cg$d_nonprolif)) < 0.2
)
```

## The EGFR-TKI non-proliferative reference number

Table 1 prints the EGFR-TKI `n_ref` as "1026". The same row prints the
ribociclib value as 1.3 x 10^7 with a superscript, so a lost superscript is the
likely cause, and the models use 10^26. That reading makes the senescence of
non-proliferative cells negligible over 96 h. Read literally as 1026 cells,
the term would remove about 45 cells per hour from the initial 230
non-proliferative cells. The vehicle non-proliferative cells would then fall
before recovering, which no panel of Figure 1E-H shows.

```{r nref-reading}
nref_compare <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  organoid_run("poziotinib", const_conc(0)) |> dplyr::mutate(reading = "1e26 (packaged)"),
  organoid_run("poziotinib", const_conc(0), params = list(nref = 1026)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(reading = "1026 (as printed)")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96)) |>
  dplyr::select(reading, time, lnonprolif)
nref_compare |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = reading, values_from = lnonprolif) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-time, \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Vehicle log10(1 + non-proliferative cells), EGFR-TKI control fit. Figure 1E-G read about 2.35, 2.5, 2.7, 2.9, 3.05.")
```

# Human epithelium: homeostasis

With no drug, the epithelium must stay at its homeostatic composition: the
transfer and shedding rates are derived so that the initial cell numbers are an
equilibrium. Villus injury stays at zero, so the diarrhea probabilities are the
baseline rates of the logistic model, `1 - expit(g0)` and `1 - expit(g2)`.

```{r steady-state}
mod_abema_h <- readModelDb("Pin_2026_abemaciclib_human")
ss <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_abema_h,
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 2000, by = 10), evid = 0, cmt = "villus", CEFFECT = 0),
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8
))
stopifnot(
  diff(range(ss$villus)) < 1e-6,
  diff(range(ss$prolif)) < 1e-6,
  max(ss$injury) < 1e-8,
  abs(ss$prob_diarrhea[1] - (1 - plogis(1.7535))) < 1e-6
)
c(baseline_any_grade = ss$prob_diarrhea[1], baseline_grade3 = ss$prob_diarrhea_grade3[1])
```

# Human abemaciclib: Figure 2B-C and Table 2

The authors deposited the Simcyp free abemaciclib profiles for 150 mg and
200 mg twice daily in enterocytes and in plasma (Data S2). The first 28 days
are supplied here at a 0.4-h step; the villus nadir falls on about day 11.

```{r abema-human}
abema_pk <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "Pin_2026_abemaciclib_simcyp.csv")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(bid150, bid200), names_to = "regimen", values_to = "CEFFECT") |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = dplyr::recode(regimen, bid150 = "150 mg BID", bid200 = "200 mg BID"))

abema_sim <- abema_pk |>
  dplyr::group_by(surrogate, regimen) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(function(d, key) {
    ev <- data.frame(id = 1, time = d$time, evid = 0, cmt = "villus", CEFFECT = d$CEFFECT)
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
      mod_abema_h, ev, covsInterpolation = "linear", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8
    )) |>
      dplyr::select(time, CEFFECT, stem, prolif, nonprolif, villus, varr, vdead,
                    injury, prob_diarrhea, prob_diarrhea_grade3)
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r abema-figure, fig.height = 5}
abema_sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Prol crypt (S + P)` = stem + prolif,
    `Villus (V + V_Arr + V_Dead)` = villus + varr + vdead
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Prol crypt (S + P)`, `Villus (V + V_Arr + V_Dead)`),
                      names_to = "cells", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, value, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(cells ~ surrogate, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Cells", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2B (plasma) and 2C (enterocyte) of Pin 2026, first 28 days.") +
  theme_bw()
```

Table 2 reports the maximum predicted villus injury and the predicted incidence
of diarrhea, taken as the maximum probability over the course of treatment.

```{r abema-table2}
table2_abema <- tibble::tribble(
  ~surrogate, ~regimen, ~injury_pub, ~any_pub, ~g34_pub,
  "enterocyte", "150 mg BID", 0.465, 64, 6,
  "enterocyte", "200 mg BID", 0.518, 78, 10,
  "plasma", "150 mg BID", 0.018, NA, NA,
  "plasma", "200 mg BID", 0.026, NA, NA
)
abema_cmp <- abema_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(surrogate, regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    injury = max(injury),
    any = 100 * max(prob_diarrhea),
    g34 = 100 * max(prob_diarrhea_grade3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(table2_abema, by = c("surrogate", "regimen"))
abema_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    injury = round(injury, 3),
    dplyr::across(c(any, g34), \(x) round(x, 0))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(surrogate, regimen, injury, injury_pub, any, any_pub, g34, g34_pub) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Surrogate = surrogate, Regimen = regimen,
    "Max injury (model)" = injury, "Max injury (Table 2)" = injury_pub,
    "Any grade % (model)" = any, "Any grade % (Table 2)" = any_pub,
    "Grade >= 3 % (model)" = g34, "Grade >= 3 % (Table 2)" = g34_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Abemaciclib: packaged human model versus Pin 2026 Table 2.")

ent <- dplyr::filter(abema_cmp, surrogate == "enterocyte")
stopifnot(
  # Injury within 3% of Table 2. The Hill coefficient of 5 steepens the
  # incidence curve, so a 1.5% injury difference moves the any-grade
  # incidence by about 2 points; the diarrhea model itself is checked
  # exactly in the next section.
  max(abs(ent$injury / ent$injury_pub - 1)) < 0.03,
  max(abs(ent$any - ent$any_pub)) < 3,
  max(abs(ent$g34 - ent$g34_pub)) < 3,
  # Plasma exposure leaves the villus essentially intact (Table 2: < 0.03).
  max(dplyr::filter(abema_cmp, surrogate == "plasma")$injury) < 0.03
)
```

# Diarrhea sub-model: Table 2 for all six drugs

The diarrhea model maps the maximum villus injury to the predicted incidence.
The check below evaluates Eq E17 with the parameter values in the packaged
model at the Table 2 enterocyte-driven injury of each regimen. The six human
model files share these values.

```{r diarrhea-table2}
ini_df <- function(model) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(model))$iniDf
th <- with(ini_df("Pin_2026_abemaciclib_human"), setNames(est, name))
diarrhea <- function(injury, g, i50) {
  hill <- injury^th[["hill_inj"]] / (injury^th[["hill_inj"]] + i50^th[["hill_inj"]])
  100 * (1 - plogis(g + th[["r_inj"]] * hill))
}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~compound, ~regimen, ~injury, ~any_pub, ~g34_pub, ~any_obs, ~g34_obs,
  "Abemaciclib", "150 mg BID", 0.465, 64, 6, 80, 9,
  "Abemaciclib", "200 mg BID", 0.518, 78, 10, 89, 19,
  "Ribociclib", "600 mg QD 3w on/1w off", 0.152, 15, 0, 15, 1,
  "Poziotinib", "16 mg QD", 0.538, 82, 11, 83, 32,
  "Lazertinib", "240 mg QD", 0.032, 15, 0, 26, 0,
  "Mobocertinib", "160 mg QD", 1.000, 96, 24, 96, 20,
  "Osimertinib", "80 mg QD", 0.440, 56, 5, 47, 1
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    any = diarrhea(injury, th[["g0"]], th[["inj50_0"]]),
    g34 = diarrhea(injury, th[["g2"]], th[["inj50_2"]])
  )
table2 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(any, g34), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::select(compound, regimen, injury, any, any_pub, any_obs, g34, g34_pub, g34_obs) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Compound = compound, Regimen = regimen, "Injury (Table 2)" = injury,
    "Any grade % (model)" = any, "Any grade % (Table 2 predicted)" = any_pub,
    "Any grade % (observed, one study)" = any_obs,
    "Grade >= 3 % (model)" = g34, "Grade >= 3 % (Table 2 predicted)" = g34_pub,
    "Grade >= 3 % (observed, one study)" = g34_obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Predicted diarrhea incidence from the Table 2 villus injury. Observed values are from one study per row; Table 2 lists every study.")

# Table 2 prints whole percentages.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(table2$any - table2$any_pub)) < 1,
  max(abs(table2$g34 - table2$g34_pub)) < 1
)
```

# Human models for the other five drugs

The Simcyp exposure profiles of ribociclib, poziotinib, lazertinib, mobocertinib
and osimertinib are shown only graphically (Figure S2) and were not deposited,
so the full Table 2 chain cannot be rerun for them. As a check that each human
file wires its own kill function, the sketch below holds the crypt exposure
constant for 28 days at 0.1, 1 and 10 times the drug's `C50kill`. Because every
drug shares the epithelial parameters, the injury at a given multiple of
`C50kill` orders the drugs by their maximal kill rate `k_kill`. A constant
exposure is far more injurious than a clinical regimen at the same peak: the
enterocyte concentration in Figure 2C stays high only for a few hours after
each dose.

```{r other-drugs}
constant_exposure <- expand.grid(drug = drugs, multiple = c(0.1, 1, 10), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    c50kill = with(ini_df(paste0("Pin_2026_", drug, "_human")), est[name == "c50kill"]),
    kkill = with(ini_df(paste0("Pin_2026_", drug, "_human")), est[name == "kkill"]),
    max_injury = {
      mod <- readModelDb(paste0("Pin_2026_", drug, "_human"))
      ev <- data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 672, by = 2), evid = 0, cmt = "villus",
                       CEFFECT = multiple * c50kill)
      max(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8))$injury)
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
constant_exposure |>
  dplyr::mutate(max_injury = round(max_injury, 3)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(drug, kkill, c50kill), names_from = multiple,
                     values_from = max_injury, names_prefix = "x") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Drug = drug, "k_kill" = kkill, "C50kill (uM)" = c50kill,
    "Max injury at 0.1 x C50" = x0.1, "at 1 x C50" = x1, "at 10 x C50" = x10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Maximum villus injury over 28 days at a constant crypt free concentration.")

at_c50 <- dplyr::filter(constant_exposure, multiple == 1)
stopifnot(
  # Same epithelium, so injury at C50kill is monotone in k_kill.
  all(diff(at_c50$max_injury[order(at_c50$kkill)]) >= 0),
  # For every drug the injury rises with the exposure multiple.
  all(tapply(constant_exposure$max_injury[order(constant_exposure$multiple)],
             constant_exposure$drug[order(constant_exposure$multiple)],
             function(x) all(diff(x) > 0)))
)
```

# Why there is no PKNCA section

The model files carry no pharmacokinetics. The drug exposure enters as an
external time-varying covariate, and the outputs are cell numbers, villus injury
and probabilities. The checks above follow the endogenous and mechanistic
validation pattern: homeostasis with no drug, then the paper's tabulated
outputs (Table 2) and the published trajectories (Figures 1 and 2).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Human epithelial constants follow the deposited code, not Table S3.**
  Table S3 lists `s_ss = 4`, `p_ss = 17.446`, `gamma = 5.31`, `m = 1.46` and
  `tau_Dead = 1/12`. The deposited MATLAB script (Data S2,
  `GI_human_Integr_Abema.m`) uses `s_ss = 2`, `p_ss = 19.446`,
  `gamma = 3.41394`, `m = 1.468566` and `tau_A = ln(2)/12`, which are the
  Gall 2023 human values. With the code values, the deposited abemaciclib
  enterocyte profiles give a maximum villus injury of 0.472 / 0.527 (0.473 /
  0.528 with the 0.4-h profiles used above) against
  0.465 / 0.518 in Table 2. With the Table S3 values the injury is
  0.349 / 0.393. Almost all of that gap comes from `gamma`. The models
  therefore use the code values, which are the values that produced the
  published results.
- **Diarrhea estimates follow the SAS output, not Table S3.** Table S3 prints
  `g0 = 2.94`, `g2 = 7.047`, `I0 = 0.2627`, `I2 = 0.22`, `r_inj = -5.56`. The SAS
  NLMIXED "Parameter Estimates" printed in the Supporting Information give
  `g0 = 1.7535`, `g12 = 6.2109`, `r_inj = -5.1074`, `Dam0_50 = 0.4818`,
  `Dam12_50 = 0.3998`. The same values are in the deposited script. Only the
  SAS values reproduce the Table 2 predicted incidences (checked above for all
  seven regimens). With the Table S3 values the abemaciclib 150 mg BID any-grade
  incidence would be 91% instead of 64%.
- **Crowding term.** Eq E15 prints the crypt crowding as
  `((S + P + D + C_Arr + C_Dead)/(s_ss + p_ss + d_ss))^m`. The deposited code
  places the arrested and dead crypt cells in the denominator instead. The
  models follow the code. For the six drugs, which induce no arrest and few
  dead crypt cells, the two forms give the same maximum injury to three
  decimals.
- **Citrulline is omitted.** The deposited human script still carries the
  Gall 2023 plasma-citrulline state. Pin 2026 neither describes nor reports it,
  so it is not in the model files; the Gall 2023 human models in this library
  include it.
- **EGFR-TKI `n_ref` read as 10^26** (see the organoid section): the printed
  "1026" contradicts Figure 1E-H.
- **Abemaciclib organoid inoculum.** Table 1 and the deposited organoid script
  start abemaciclib from 1993 proliferative and 1110 non-proliferative cells,
  but Figure 1C starts from about 10^2.74 and 10^2.36 cells (the EGFR-TKI
  inoculum, 553 / 230). The paper notes that experiment-specific inoculum sizes
  were used. The model files keep the Table 1 values as `p0` / `n0`; the
  Figure 1 replication above overrides them.
- **Figure 1H (osimertinib).** The vehicle arm in Figure 1H rises to about
  10^3.65 proliferative cells and starts from about 10^2.65 non-proliferative
  cells, unlike the shared EGFR-TKI control fit in Table 1 (about 10^3.2 at
  96 h). The osimertinib panel appears to come from a separate control fit that
  the paper does not tabulate. The packaged osimertinib drug arm still ends
  close to the figure (log10 values 2.55 and 2.59 against about 2.5 and 2.6).
- **Figure 1F (lazertinib).** At the labelled 60 nM the Table 1 lazertinib
  kill function lowers the 96-h counts by about 0.11 (proliferative) and
  0.14 (non-proliferative) log units against the vehicle. Figure 1F draws a
  drop of about 0.3 log units for both. The label may give the nominal rather
  than the measured medium concentration. The measured lazertinib profile was
  not deposited, so the panel cannot be rerun, and the Table 1 values are kept.
- **Arrest function.** Table 1 reports `k_arrest = 0` for all six drugs and
  gives no arrest `C50` or Hill coefficient. The models keep the arrest pathway
  (Eqs 5, E11-E12), with `c50arrest = 1` and `hillarrest = 1` taken from the
  placeholders in the deposited code; they have no effect while `karrest = 0`.
- **Kill-function precision.** Table 1 prints the abemaciclib kill parameters
  as 1.90 and 3.51 uM; the deposited scripts carry 1.9021 and 3.5143. The
  models use the Table 1 values for all six drugs.
- **Exposure surrogate.** The crypt free concentration is not measurable. The
  authors bracketed it between the Simcyp-predicted free plasma and free
  enterocyte (ileum I) concentrations and concluded the enterocyte surrogate
  predicts the clinical incidence. The Simcyp PBPK models are not reproduced;
  users supply `CEFFECT` from their own exposure model. Physicochemical and
  ADME inputs are listed in Tables S1-S2.
- **Mobocertinib regimen.** Table 2 lists mobocertinib at 120 and 160 mg once
  daily; the Figure 2G legend reads "BID". Table 2 is followed here.
- **Deterministic typical-value models.** No inter-individual variability and
  no residual error are reported, so the files carry none. The organoid fits
  used log-transformed counts with weighted least squares (Supporting
  Information fit statistics).
- No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-13.
